# Quick Brief: Exit-Ticket Frequency Decision

## Summary

The alpha team's classroom trial found daily two-question exit tickets improve retention of covered material [1]. Completion stays under three minutes when the ticket holds two questions [3]. Weekly checks suit content that changes little between lessons [1]. The deciding factor is how often new material introduces confusion, and the retention data favours the daily cadence with a strict question cap.

## Key Points

- Daily two-question exit tickets improve retention of covered material in observed classrooms [2].
- Completion stays under three minutes when the ticket holds two questions [3].
- The deciding factor is how often new material introduces confusion.

## Action Items

- Adopt daily exit tickets with a maximum of two questions.
- Review the weekly aggregate every Friday during planning period.
- Revisit the decision at half term with the retention data.

## Bibliography

[1] Alpha Analytics (2024). "Retention pace in classroom practice". https://example.com/alpha
[2] Beta Education Notes (2023). "Time cost of formative checks". https://example.com/beta
[3] Gamma Teaching Quarterly (2022). "Feedback frequency for stable curricula". https://example.com/gamma
